key_insight: A lightweight Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) approach built on a Temporal Convolutional Network enables on-device, low-cost adaptation to EMG signal drift so gesture-recognition accuracy is maintained over time.
problem_solved: Long-term EMG decoding degrades due to electrode shifts, muscle fatigue, and posture changes; this paper addresses maintaining robust gesture recognition without large retraining pipelines or heavy compute unsuitable for wearables.
method: Compact Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) as an EMG time-series backbone optimized for low compute.
Test-time adaptation that updates a small set of parameters (e.g., normalization or lightweight adapter layers) using unlabeled/test-time signals rather than full re-training.
Design choices focused on energy- and memory-efficiency (few update steps, small buffers) so adaptation can run on battery-constrained wearable devices.
impact: Makes continuous, robust EMG-based gesture recognition practical on resource-constrained wearables by reducing recalibration needs and avoiding large labeled datasets or cloud compute, accelerating real-world deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: wearable sensor → lightweight TCN → small adaptation module updating on-device at test time
Before/After bar chart: recognition accuracy drop over time without TTA vs. maintained accuracy with the proposed TTA
Icon set: wearable device (low-power), stopwatch (real-time/low latency), battery (energy efficiency)
Resource vs. performance plot: computation/energy cost on x-axis and accuracy/robustness on y-axis showing favorable tradeoff
paper_title: Lightweight Test-Time Adaptation for EMG-Based Gesture Recognition
paper_authors: Nia Touko, Matthew O A Ellis, Cristiano Capone, Alessio Burrello, Elisa Donati
